chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Raib, from Ismail ibn ibn al-Fazl, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you rise in the morning and when you settle in the evening, say ten times: 'O Allah, whatever blessing or health of religion or world has come to me, it is from You Alone, there is no partner for You. To You is the praise and to You is the gratitude for it upon me, O Lord, until You are pleased, and after the pleasure.'
For indeed, when you say that, you have fulfilled the gratitude for whatever Allah has favored you with, during that day and during that night.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended morning and evening supplication for gratitude in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes this specific supplication to be recited ten times in the morning and evening, emphasizing the Shia emphasis on structured, daily remembrance (dhikr) as a means of spiritual maintenance. The du'a comprehensively attributes all blessings of religion (din) and the world (dunya) solely to Allah, concluding with a request for divine pleasure (rida) that extends beyond mere satisfaction. Reciting this is considered the fulfillment of gratitude (shukr) for the day's and night's favors, linking verbal acknowledgment with the internal state of contentment.
